summary: Sega's Formula One-inspired racing line, from the TTL-based Monaco GP arcade cabinet through Super Monaco GP and Ayrton Senna's licensed sequel.

entries.title: Monaco GP
entries.definitive_edition: Sega Ages 2500 Series Vol. 2: Monaco GP / Sega Classics Collection

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware for the remake; use MAME/original hardware for the arcade Monaco GP and Pro Monaco GP preservation route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: PS2 remake visuals for main route; original cabinet controls and LEDs only on arcade hardware

primary.version: Sega Ages 2500 Series Vol. 2: Monaco GP / Sega Classics Collection remake
primary.why: The original Monaco GP is an important TTL-based arcade game with cockpit cabinet variants, but Sega's 2003 PlayStation 2 remake adds more cars and game modes. For a best-version guide focused on fidelity and completeness, the PlayStation 2 remake is the most complete route, while the arcade original remains the preservation/authenticity reference.
primary.how_to_play: Play Sega Ages 2500 Series Vol. 2: Monaco GP on Japanese PlayStation 2, or Sega Classics Collection on PlayStation 2 where available; preserve the original arcade cabinet separately for historical authenticity.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PlayStation 2 release is a remake, not a pure arcade preservation release; use arcade hardware/emulation if the goal is the original TTL cabinet experience.

entries.title: Super Monaco GP
entries.definitive_edition: Original arcade deluxe cabinet for fidelity; Genesis/Mega Drive for home-exclusive championship content

emulation.notes: Use MAME or original arcade hardware for the primary; use Genesis/Mega Drive emulation or hardware for World Championship secondary content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sega X Board 60 fps arcade output with cabinet force feedback and Air Drive only on original hardware

primary.version: Original Sega X Board arcade release, preferably deluxe Air Drive cabinet
primary.why: Super Monaco GP began as a Sega X Board arcade game with 60 fps output, force-feedback steering, Fresnel lens display enlargement, Air Drive seat motion on the deluxe cabinet, and linked-cabinet multiplayer. Home versions add World Championship and extra tracks, so the arcade is the fidelity route while Genesis/Sega CD-style home content is a secondary completion route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; use a deluxe Air Drive cabinet where possible, then sample the Genesis or Sega CD home version for World Championship content.

secondary.exclusive_content: World Championship mode with multiple 1989 Formula One World Championship-style tracks, team progression, and password saves.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the World Championship mode after the arcade primary if you want the home-exclusive long-form season structure.
secondary.why: The arcade has the best cabinet fidelity; Sega added more tracks and modes to compensate for the home versions' lack of cabinet engagement.

entries.remaster_caveats: Sega CD compilation uses the Genesis port rather than a new arcade-perfect version.

entries.title: Ayrton Senna's Super Monaco GP II

emulation.notes: Use accurate Genesis/Mega Drive emulation or original hardware.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original 16-bit console presentation with modern scaling

primary.why: Ayrton Senna's Super Monaco GP II was developed for Genesis/Mega Drive, Master System, and Game Gear with Ayrton Senna's endorsement and technical input. The Genesis/Mega Drive version is the highest-fidelity release among the sourced platforms and contains the championship and Senna GP structure.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version on original hardware or a compatible emulator such as Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, or MiSTer.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster; this is a distinct sequel to Super Monaco GP, not a port of the 1989 arcade game.
